Are you curious about how complex machines are built, and do you enjoy turning technical details into practical solutions on the shop floor? • A hands-on learning role where you work close to the product, the people and the daily assembly process.

• The chance to make a visible difference by supporting better documentation, smoother workflows and practical improvements.

• A development-oriented role where you can grow your manufacturing engineering skills step by step.

Hands on experience in digital product development, UX, service design or consulting.

The ability to combine creative exploration with analytical and structured thinking, translating complex challenges and research findings into clear recommendations and concepts.

Do you enjoy working in a close team where quality, safety, and flexibility truly matter? Are you curious by nature, technically inclined, and passionate about creating a safe and efficient working environment? Then this might be your next step.

We are now looking for a Terminal Operator with a particular responsibility for safety management to strengthen our team in Frederikshavn. This role is ideal for someone who wants to be part of a dynamic shipping environment, take an active role in developing our safety culture, and contribute to the future of terminal and bunker operations.

**Why This Role Is Different

**This is not a one-track job. As a terminal operator, you will combine hands-on operational work with administrative, technical, and safety management responsibilities. You will be part of a small team where each individual contributes with their own strengths, whether within engineering, maintenance, safety management, electrical work, or operational coordination.

You will share daily tasks and responsibilities with your colleagues while taking particular ownership of the terminal's safety management, promoting safe working practices, and contributing to the continuous improvement of our operations.

**Your Day-to-Day Impact

**Together with your colleagues, you will:

• Support safe and efficient cargo handling and storage operations

• Supervise the technical and safety condition of the terminal

• Coordinate and develop the terminal's safety management practices

• Promote a proactive safety culture and encourage safe working behaviours

• Coordinate risk assessments, safety inspections, emergency preparedness, and incident follow-up

• Support compliance with applicable regulatory, industry, and company requirements

• Work in shifts with shared operational responsibility

• Operate both independently and as part of a team, depending on the situation

**Beyond the Terminal

**In addition to managing the terminal, we also operate a fleet of highly modern bunker tankers.

During periods of low terminal activity or when rapid response is required, you may support our shipping operations. This can include assisting with immediate repairs, handling administrative tasks, supporting safety-related activities, or assisting with crew changes and operational coordination.

**Who You Are

**You thrive in an environment where things move quickly, and priorities may change at short notice. You remain calm under pressure, adapt easily, and are comfortable working outside normal office hours.

You have a genuine interest in operational safety and understand the importance of translating safety requirements into practical and effective working practices. You are comfortable taking responsibility, leading by example, and engaging colleagues in continuous improvement.

You are someone who:

• Is passionate about your work and enjoys variety

• Demonstrates a proactive approach to safety and risk management

• Takes ownership and leads by example

• Handles change without becoming stressed

• Appreciates structured processes while remaining flexible

• Is proactive, reliable, and solution-oriented

**Your Background

**We value experience, but we value motivation and willingness to learn just as highly.

Marine experience is highly desirable, preferably in the capacity of a deck officer. Experience from tanker operations, cargo handling, ship-shore interfaces, and maritime safety management is considered particularly valuable.

We welcome applicants with backgrounds such as:

• Marine experience, preferably as a deck officer

• Terminal operations and safety management

• Cargo surveying

• HSSEQ or operational risk management

• Technical, electrical, maintenance, or other safety-related roles

You should be able to communicate clearly in English and one Scandinavian language, both spoken and written, and have completed at least high school education.

You will be surrounded by experienced colleagues who are committed to supporting your development and helping you build new skills, both within terminal operations and safety management.

**About OljOla Shipping and Terminals

**OljOla Shipping and Terminals is an established company within the tanker shipping industry, founded in 1978 with roots on Donsö Island. We specialise in the distribution of bunkers and operate a highly modern fleet of bunker tankers.

Our ambition is to become a leading bunker and terminal operator through strong operational efficiency, technical innovation, safety, and sustainability.

jobs.occupation: Chief Consultant in Systemic Approaches to Sustainability at Department of Agroecology, Aarhus University
jobs.description:
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for the position of Chief Consultant to support and advance the development of sustainable business plans for the Global Rust Reference Centre (GRRC) at Aarhus University in collaboration with NordGen. The position is open from 1 February 2027 for a duration of three years.

Objectives
• Develop roadmaps for future governance, collaboration and funding models.
• Coordinate negotiations and multi-country partnership building across institutions and agricultural and business sectors.

Key Responsibilities
• Propose governance and management model options based on stakeholder, governance and mandate mapping.
• Document stakeholder and partner universe and develop a plan of how to engage them on what.
• Design a long-term fundraising strategy and associated roadmap.
• Attract funding in the short-term to sustain GRRC research, early warning services and services to plant resistance breeding.

Qualifications
We are looking for a candidate with:

• Demonstrated experience with management and governance of global agricultural research programmes and development of research funding strategies.
• Demonstrated experience with development of research strategy change focusing on research impact and partnership management.
• Demonstrated ability to translate complex issues and scientific challenges into actionable development strategies and solutions.
• An extensive professional network and demonstrated ability to engage across academia, Private Public Partnerships, public and private funders, regulatory bodies, and industry sectors.

Who we are
At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 400 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.

We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme

Living and working in Denmark
• Subsidised childcare and free education from primary school through university.
• Universal healthcare for you and your family as residents.
• Five weeks of paid holiday per year.
• Generous parental leave – up to 52 weeks shared between parents, with full or partial salary.

Startdate and duration of employment
The position is open from 1 February 2027 for a duration of three years.

Place of Work
The place of work is Aarhus University, Research Centre Flakkebjerg. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

More information can be obtained from Head of Department Jørgen E. Olesen, jeo@agro.au.dk 

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as a Chief Consultant, with remuneration in accordance with Appendix 4 of the collective agreement.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk
